titulo: My Grandpa Called Me. Three Days After His Funeral | Urban Legend #Shorts
titulo_pt: Meu avô me ligou. Três dias depois do enterro | Lenda urbana
resumo_pt: Lenda das ligações dos mortos. Três dias depois do enterro do avô, o telefone fixo da casa dele toca de madrugada enquanto a narradora arruma as coisas. É a voz dele: 'Sai de casa agora. Não acende nada.' Ela sai, e os bombeiros acham um vazamento de gás na cozinha. A companhia telefônica confirma: aquela linha estava cortada desde o dia do enterro.
descricao:
The phone line had been dead for days.

Would you have answered?

Follow @VeilFrequency for a new horror story every day. Based on a classic American urban legend. Images are AI-generated.

scenes.text: My grandpa died in October. I was the one who stayed to clean out his house.
scenes.pt: Meu avô morreu em outubro. Fui eu que fiquei pra esvaziar a casa dele.
scenes.visual: old farmhouse at dusk, cardboard boxes on the porch

scenes.text: He still had an old phone on the kitchen wall. The kind with a curly cord.
scenes.pt: Ele ainda tinha um telefone velho na parede da cozinha. Daqueles de fio enrolado.
scenes.visual: old rotary wall phone with a curly cord in a dim kitchen

scenes.text: On the third night, I fell asleep on his couch.
scenes.pt: Na terceira noite, dormi no sofá dele.
scenes.visual: woman asleep on an old couch under a knitted blanket, lamp off

scenes.text: At two a.m., that phone started ringing.
scenes.pt: Às duas da manhã, aquele telefone começou a tocar.

scenes.text: I picked it up half asleep. Hello?
scenes.visual: woman holding an old phone receiver to her ear in a dark kitchen

scenes.text: I couldn't breathe. It was his voice. The cough. The way he said sweetheart.
scenes.pt: Eu não conseguia respirar. Era a voz dele. A tosse. O jeito que ele falava querida.
scenes.visual: close up of a trembling hand gripping a phone cord

scenes.text: Get out of the house. Right now. Don't turn on any lights.
scenes.pt: Sai de casa. Agora. Não acende nenhuma luz.

scenes.visual: phone receiver hanging by its cord in a dark kitchen

scenes.text: I didn't think. I ran outside barefoot in the dark.
scenes.pt: Não pensei. Corri pra fora descalça, no escuro.
scenes.visual: barefoot woman running out of a farmhouse door at night

scenes.text: From the yard, I called nine-one-one.
scenes.visual: woman standing in a dark yard holding a glowing cell phone

scenes.text: The firefighters found a gas leak in the kitchen. The whole house was full of it.
scenes.pt: Os bombeiros acharam um vazamento de gás na cozinha. A casa inteira estava cheia.
scenes.visual: firefighters with flashlights inside an old kitchen at night

scenes.text: One light switch, and it would've exploded.
scenes.pt: Um interruptor, e tudo teria explodido.
scenes.visual: close up of an old light switch on a kitchen wall

scenes.text: The next morning, I called the phone company to ask who called me.
scenes.pt: Na manhã seguinte, liguei pra companhia telefônica pra perguntar quem tinha me ligado.
scenes.visual: woman at a kitchen table with coffee and a cell phone, morning light

scenes.text: Nobody did. That line was disconnected the day of his funeral.
scenes.pt: Ninguém. Aquela linha foi cortada no dia do enterro dele.
scenes.visual: old wall phone with its cord unplugged, morning light

scenes.text: I kept that phone. It's on my kitchen wall now. Just in case.
scenes.pt: Eu fiquei com aquele telefone. Agora ele está na parede da minha cozinha. Só por garantia.
scenes.visual: old rotary phone hanging on a modern kitchen wall

personagens: the narrator is a woman in her twenties with short black hair and a gray hoodie; grandpa is an old man with a white beard, round glasses and a plaid shirt; the phone is an old yellow rotary wall phone
